title: Battery storage facility approved on Guelph Street
subtitle: Operations centre construction budget, Elora paid parking, water and wastewater plan, recreation priority registration and road tenders.
overview: Council supported a battery energy storage facility at 6235 Guelph Street, Nichol. It approved the rezoning and recommended that the County adopt the related Official Plan Amendment {{vote:m3}}. Staff said concerns could be handled through site plan approval and legal agreements. The zoning by-law will return for enactment after the County acts.

Council approved the guaranteed maximum price and construction budget for the new Operations Centre, with substantial completion expected by December 2026. Staff will also look at solar options, apply for a federal fleet electrification grant, and investigate a $33.9 million debt issue. Staff said the project should not affect the tax levy.

Council directed staff to start a downtown paid parking program in Elora and to contract with Alpha Parking Solutions. It also adopted a recreation priority registration policy for township residents and awarded tenders for Colborne Street reconstruction and a chlorine storage room upgrade.
Council received the draft Water and Wastewater Servicing Master Plan for information. Staff are to return on June 16 seeking endorsement of the preferred option for the Fergus wastewater plant.

decisions.detail: Council approved rezoning for a battery energy storage system and recommended the County adopt the matching Official Plan Amendment {{vote:m3}}.

decisions.item: New Operations Centre price and financing
decisions.detail: Council approved the guaranteed maximum price and construction budget with Ball Construction Ltd., directed construction to proceed, and directed staff to investigate a $33.9 million debt issue plus solar and fleet-electrification grant options.
Council authorized staff to start a paid parking program in downtown Elora and delegated authority to negotiate and sign a contract with Alpha Parking Solutions.
Council approved a policy giving township residents early access to program registration, and approved a revised RZone Respect and Responsibility Policy.
Council awarded Tender #33-25 to Drexler Construction Limited at $2,199,154.08 including contingency, excluding HST, with project funding updated.

decisions.item: Well FPH1 chlorine storage room tender
decisions.detail: Council awarded Tender #12-25 to Xterra Construction Inc. at $236,141.53 excluding HST and updated project funding.

decisions.item: Development charge deferral for a manufacturer
decisions.detail: Council authorized a development charge deferral payment agreement with Assiduos Holdings Ltd. (Xanadu Homes Ltd.).

debate: On the battery facility, the landowners and a skilled-trades union spoke in support, citing farm viability, local jobs and grid reliability. One councillor opposed it, citing resident opposition, the size and location, foreign-backed ownership, and fire, noise and air-quality risks.

Councillors asked about landscaping, the on-site fire water tank, extra batteries added over time, insurance and who bears costs if problems arise. Staff said details come at site plan, which staff now approve. A separate community benefits agreement would come to council.

Supporters said the 200-metre setback and fire department input addressed safety, and that the need for energy storage was large. Another councillor said ownership should not matter given regulatory standards.

On the Operations Centre, one councillor asked whether Bill 17 changes to development charges put the debt plan at risk. Staff said it had other tools to adjust and expected no tax levy impact. Councillors also asked about the market for surplus property sales and non-core items such as the pavilion and greenhouse.

On paid parking, councillors asked about more accessible spaces, a daycare drop-off zone, whether turnover would improve if workers buy long-term passes, and downtown residents needing to move cars every 24 hours. Staff said township residents would park free and Fergus would not have paid parking.
